WORLD: A Levantine graphic tradition carried in the owner's own primary: flat fully-saturated colour used as whole fields rather than accents, a bilingual lockup that sets Arabic and Latin as equals, and the numeral on the back of a shirt. The primary is #91338A, with #26202C as the ground the dark theme is built on. Recorded in full in .impeccable/surfaces/admin.md.

Type, palette, density and one signature move. It never supplies the layout, the navigation model or the controls, which stay standard web components. A crest, a stripe, a mascot or a shirt texture would be the costume rather than the grammar, and none ships.

The monumental numeral. Every quantity the operator reads first is set in Archivo at type.figure on a baseline with its unit and its provenance beneath, never inside a bordered tile. A figure is the content, not an ornament on it.

Colour appears only inside a region that is doing a job: the shell, a category field, a state, a data series, or selection. It is never scattered over the page as decoration. The primary is reserved for the brand's own two jobs -- the shell field and what can be pressed -- and a disabled action loses it.

The neutrals carry the primary's cast rather than a grey or a green one, so a page with no colour on it still reads as this product. The dark theme is #26202C's family all the way down. What is deliberately outside the family is the five status hues, because a state the eye reads as the brand is a state nobody notices.

Screenprint on textile: matte, opaque, no gradient, no glass, no glow, no halo. Depth comes from a 2px rule and a solid field, not from a shadow. The one shadow in the system carries a real offset and blur and belongs to overlays only.
DARK_RAMP: Dark canvas floor, the shell field and inputs. The darkest member of the primary's own family, not neutral black.
Dark cards, panels, table bodies. The owner's dark primary, placed where it covers the most of the screen a reader actually looks at.
Dark overlays, popovers, dropdowns, and the current item on the shell field.
Dark secondary text. Tinted from the primary's own hue rather than grey.
Dark warning and the wordmark mark.
Dark info, filed and recorded. Steel lifted for a ground built on #26202C.
Dark success and the staffing category field.
Dark AI. Guardrail G7 keeps this system-owned in both themes.
SEMANTIC: App background. The field everything sits on.
Cards, panels, table bodies, sheets. In dark this is #26202C itself: the owner's dark primary on the largest readable area rather than on one panel.
Table headers, inset wells, log areas.
Selected row, active tab, current nav item.
The scrim behind a sheet or dialog.
Supporting copy, provenance lines, column headers.
Captions and placeholders. The lightest text permitted below 18.66px.
Disabled controls only. Never placeholders: see CONTRAST.

Text on a filled action or a saturated field. **It is bone in both themes now, which it was not before.** The action fill used to be ink in light and bone in dark, so the label had to flip with it; the fill is a plum in both themes now, so the label does not. One value is the fact rather than an oversight.

Text on a field that is bright in both themes -- the money category field is gold.400 in light and gold.light in dark, and both take ink at 9.43:1 and better. White on it is 2.04:1, the one pairing in this palette that looks deliberate and fails.
Inline links. Always underlined; colour is never the only signal.
Input borders, card edges, table rules.

The 2px rule. The structural line, not a hairline -- and the thing that separates a large colour field from the canvas behind it, where a contrast ratio between two fields is not the right instrument.
Focus ring. Maximum contrast in both themes, drawn with a 2px offset so it survives on a filled action. Guardrail G4: never configurable.
The border of a field that failed validation.

Primary action fill. **The owner's #91338A, and the reason it can be is G2.** The action colour was ink because the shell field and the success state were both the same green, so a saturated action would have shared a hue with a status. The primary shares a hue with nothing in this palette -- 51 degrees from error, 97 from warning, 148 from success, 108 from info, 73 from AI -- so the one pressable thing on the page is the brand itself. bone on it is 6.90:1 light and 4.91:1 dark; the fill clears its canvas by 6.02:1 and 3.63:1.

Primary action, hovered. A declared token rather than a filter, because the retired rule was brightness(0.95) and that is one step per channel on a dark fill -- no hover state at all on the page's primary action. Light deepens, dark lifts.

Succeeded, active, paid, present. **Green stays, and only here.** It is a status rather than an identity: a paid invoice rendered in the brand colour would be a state the eye reads as a highlight, and this is the one job the retired green was doing that the primary cannot take over.

Failed, refused, overdue, at risk. **Moved to a true red.** The retired error was a claret at 342 degrees, which sits 37 degrees from the new primary -- close enough that a refusal and the brand would have read as one family on a page carrying both. 356 degrees separates them.

AI interpretation, recommendation and evidence. Guardrail G7: system-owned. **Moved from 247 to 232 degrees** for the same reason the error moved: a violet-indigo beside a plum primary is two purples, and G7 asks for a role nothing else can be mistaken for.
The ground of an AI region.
The edge of an AI region.
The shell field: the navigation rail and the sign-in panel. The one large committed colour, and in light it is the primary's own deep end.
The current item's ground on the shell field. A tint of the field rather than a bar down one side of it: the craft floor bans the one-sided bar and offers a tint as the alternative.
Group headings and secondary text on the shell field. Tinted from the field's own hue rather than grey, which is what the craft floor asks for on a coloured surface. 5.94:1 light, 9.33:1 dark.

Text on the current item's ground. Declared per theme rather than reusing color.text.inverse: on the dark theme's selected ground an inverted value was 1.94:1 once, a real failure. 9.45:1 light, 12.57:1 dark.
The wordmark's mark and the current-item marker on the shell field. Gold against the plum field rather than in it, which is the one place two committed colours meet on purpose.
Retention: expiring memberships, cancellations, leads going cold.
Staffing and delivery: rotas, unstaffed classes, devices.
Text on the money field. Gold is light in both themes, so ink in both: 9.43:1 light, 11.27:1 dark. White on it is 2.04:1.
Text on the compliance field. Steel is dark in light and a light tint in dark, so the text flips: bone 5.74:1, then ink 9.60:1.
Text on the retention field. Crimson flips the same way: bone 7.48:1, then ink 7.41:1.
Text on the staffing field. Turf flips the same way: bone 6.81:1, then ink 9.94:1.
TYPE_SCALE: The signature move. One quantity the operator reads first, set on a baseline with its unit and provenance beneath. Never inside a bordered tile, and never more than one register of it per region.
A secondary quantity in the same baseline, and the figure a phone collapses to.
The opening sentence of a surface that leads with a verdict.
Section heading, sheet title, member name in a record header.
The smallest heading. Table group headers.
Reading copy on a surface at Spacious density.
Field labels, column headers, the unit under a figure. Never a kicker above a heading.
Provenance and footnotes. Latin only; Arabic resolves to 13px.
Tabular figures inside a grid. Archivo's tabular set, not a monospace costume.
FACES: Self-hosted by next/font at build time, declared in src/app/layout.tsx. A grotesque with the flat confident numerals of a shirt number: it holds at 72px and still aligns in a table at 13.5. Carries type.figure, type.figureSm, type.display, type.h1 and every tabular figure.
Self-hosted by next/font at build time. A workhorse UI face at the sizes this product reads at, with the slightly condensed set width a dense operations screen needs.

Self-hosted by next/font at build time. A Kufi-influenced grotesque that sits beside Archivo and Barlow without a seam, and is regionally credible. Carries both Arabic text and Arabic display, and ships the tabular figures a mirrored column needs.

The old system set every figure in a monospace face. Monospace is for code, not for 'technical'; tabular alignment is Archivo's tabular-figure feature, which aligns without borrowing a typewriter's voice.

GUARDRAILS: G1
brand.accent must reach 4.5:1 against surface.default and surface.canvas, and its computed on-accent label colour must reach 4.5:1 against the accent itself.
Rejected at upload with the nearest passing value offered.
G2
brand.accent must sit a minimum perceptual distance from success, warning and error. A brand green close to success is refused.

This system resolves the same problem for itself rather than only for tenants, and the primary is what resolved it. The retired shell colour and the success state were both the same green, so a saturated action would have shared a hue with a status and the action had to be ink instead. #91338A shares a hue with nothing: 51 degrees from error, 73 from AI, 97 from warning, 108 from info, 148 from success. So the primary is the shell field *and* the one pressable thing on the page, which is what the owner asked for and what the old palette could not have given.
G3
brand.accent may never resolve into a status, money-state, safety or consent token. Enforced by the token boundary — the accent is simply not in scope for those components.
Not surfaced to the tenant.
G4
The focus ring is system-owned in both themes.
Not configurable. A tenant cannot ship an unnavigable product. Drawn as 2px with a 2px offset so it survives on a filled action, where a ring in the action's own colour would vanish.
G5
Dark-mode accent is derived from brand.accent, not configured separately.
Not surfaced. Prevents a tenant passing light mode and failing dark, which is the most common white-label accessibility failure.
G6
Logo requires a monochrome fallback before a brand can publish.
Blocks publish rather than degrading silently on receipts, invoices and exports.
G7
color.semantic.ai is system-owned in both themes and is not in scope for brand.accent.
AI interpretation, recommendation, evidence and executed-action states resolve to ai.* regardless of tenant branding.
ARABIC_RULES: At any given size, Arabic gets 0.15 more line-height than Latin — type.body is 1.60 in Latin and 1.75 in Arabic. Diacritics and descenders need the room, and dense Arabic without it reads as a solid block.
Arabic never renders below 13px. type.caption (11.5) is a Latin-only token; its Arabic counterpart resolves to 13px. A caption that cannot be read is not a caption.
Cairo reads optically lighter than Barlow at the same weight. Where Latin uses 400, Arabic uses 400; where Latin uses 500 or 600, Arabic uses 600; where Latin uses 700, Arabic uses 700.
Never apply tracking to Arabic — it breaks the joins. Any token carrying a track value drops it in Arabic, which is why type.label resolves to zero tracking in Arabic.
Arabic has no italic convention. Emphasis is weight or colour. Any component using italics for meaning must have a non-italic Arabic path.
Arabic runs 15–30% longer than English here. Every label container, button and column is dimensioned against the Arabic string, not the English one.
Figures are Archivo, Arabic text is Cairo
Cairo carries Arabic-Indic numerals; Archivo carries Latin ones. A tabular column in an Arabic table switches family but keeps its alignment and width, because both faces ship tabular figures.

Latin or Arabic-Indic, chosen once per tenant and applied identically on screen, receipt, export and PDF. Never mixed within a tenant, and never decided per component. Money figures and identifiers a reader cites stay Latin.
Money, phone numbers, member IDs, card last-four, times and Latin names are each wrapped in an isolated run. Without it JOD jumps to the wrong side of its amount.
THEMES: A back office with the lights on, read for hours at a stretch. Bone is a cleaner ground than warm paper for saturated category fields, which go muddy over cream. Dark ships as a true theme for early and late work, not a courtesy, and it is built on #26202C rather than on black.
Lobbies are bright, the screen is read at 1.5m, and staff do not choose their lighting. Dark would cost contrast headroom at exactly the moment resolution speed matters.
Gym-floor lighting swings from window glare to dim free-weight corners. This is the surface where user control genuinely earns its keep.
Consumer expectation, plus evening and pre-dawn training. Dark is a first-class member experience here.
Operated at night during incidents, beside other operations tooling. The one surface where dark is the default rather than the alternative.
CHARACTER: Colour arrives as whole fields -- a plum rail, a gold block, a crimson block -- not as an accent sprinkled on grey. A grey screen with one accent colour is the category default without the category's polish, and this system refuses it.

The quantity the operator came for is set at 72px on a baseline, not shrunk into a tile with a label above it. Scale is the hierarchy; a border around a number is a substitute for deciding it matters.

Screenprint, not glass. No gradient, no blur, no glow, no coloured halo. The structural line is a 2px rule in ink, and the only shadow in the system belongs to an overlay and carries a real offset and blur.
Arabic and Latin are set as equals in one lockup, and every container is dimensioned against the Arabic string. Parity is structural here, not a translation pass at the end.

Where a figure cannot be derived, the surface says which fact is missing and what would supply it — in the operator's language, in one line, in the place the figure would have been. It never prints a plausible number, and it never explains itself to engineers on a working screen.

Colour appears only where it is doing a job. The action colour marks what can be pressed and nothing else; a disabled action loses it; a category field carries one kind of concern and does not leak into another.

Columns never move. Data changes inside a fixed grid, a row that reranks keeps its identity, and a row that changed holds its marker until it has been seen. A layout that reflows under new data is a layout the operator has to re-read.

34px rows where scanning is the job, tabular figures that align without effort, one authored motion moment rather than an entrance on every section. Speed is a visual property here, not only a performance one.
BRANDABLE: A tenant's single accent, bounded by G1, G2 and G3.
Resolves into links, selection and the current-item marker. Never into a status, money, safety or consent token.
A tenant wordmark with a required monochrome fallback (G6).
Replaces the Veyro lockup on the shell field and on exports.
Whether the shell field takes the tenant accent or stays plum.
Bounded by the same contrast rule as the accent: the computed on-field text must reach 4.5:1.
success, warning, error, info and ai are system-owned in both themes.
A tenant recolouring 'overdue' is a tenant shipping a safety defect.
DENSITY: Admin data grids, Console tenant lists, financial ledgers. Maximum rows per screen where scanning is the job.
Admin detail views, record inspectors, CRM, settings, forms.
Coach app, Front Desk, Kiosk, POS register. Never user-selectable on Front Desk or Kiosk.
Member app. Plus type.display and space.16 for first-run, milestones and progress moments.
BREAKPOINTS: Single column. The surface collapses to the single next decision with its figure monumental. Tables become drill-down lists, never shrunken grids.
Tablet portrait. Front Desk minimum. Rail collapses to icons.
Tablet landscape and small laptop. Admin usable: rail collapsed, inspector becomes an overlay rather than a column.
Admin target. Rail expanded at 240, content and inspector side by side.
Wide desktop. Content caps at 1440 and centres; the inspector widens to 480 rather than the table stretching indefinitely.
SHELL: px, icons only, from bp.sm down.
px. Content caps and centres rather than stretching.
px. The world's structural line weight.
LAYOUTS: A pitch-green rail down the inside edge carrying the bilingual lockup and navigation grouped by what the operator is trying to do, over a bone field. Split view is list plus inspector, never three columns.
Two zones, no rail: a fixed capture strip at the top holding scan and search, and a resolution area below. Touch density, one modal depth maximum, keyboard focus returning to the scan field.
Single column, bottom nav of four plus a create action. Sheets capped at two levels. Primary actions in the lower third for one-handed reach. Two-pane only from bp.sm on tablet.
Single column, Spacious. Bottom nav of five. One 'now' card owning the top of the viewport; everything else below the fold.
The Admin shell at Compact density on the dark theme, with an incident banner slot above the rail that no other surface has.
MOTION: A surface gets one motion idea, not an entrance on every section. On Admin it is the queue: a row that reranks moves to its new position rather than disappearing and reappearing, and keeps its identity while it travels.
Everything animates from an already-visible default. Content never fades in from nothing, because a page that assembles itself is a page the operator waits for.
120ms for a control's own feedback, 200ms for a surface change, 320ms for a row travelling. Nothing is slower than 320ms on a working screen.
prefers-reduced-motion removes travel and cross-fades and keeps state changes instant. A change marker is a colour and a rule, never only a movement, so nothing is lost.
